title: Two Fires In Belfast Over One October Weekend Left One Dead And Seven Displaced
text:
Maine State Fire Marshals Investigate 2 Separate Fires In Belfast This Weekend, One Was Fatal
Two separate fires, one on Friday and another on Saturday, brought Maine State Fire Marshal Investigators to the Belfast area over the weekend.
Fire #1
The first fire took place on Friday, October 30th, just after 2:30 PM on Back Searsport Road.
The Belfast Fire Department responded to a mobile home that had caught fire. While they battled the flames, they discovered human remains inside the home.
Read More: Generator Enclosed In Box Sparked West Bath Halloween Fire
According to the Maine Department of Public Safety, fire marshal investigators were able to narrow down the area in which the blaze began, but are still not sure what started it.
Read More: cause of Presque Isle Apartment House Fire Released
"Investigators have narrowed the area of origin to a rear porch that contained a laundry area....Investigators examined the scene and recovered the deceased individual from the debris...The deceased individual was transported to the Office of the Chief Medical Examiner in Augusta, where an examination will be conducted to confirm the individual’s identity and determine the cause of death."
We're told two dogs also died in this fire. They are still trying to determine how the fire started.
Fire #2
The next evening, on Saturday, October 31st, just after 5 PM, Belfast firefighters were called to an apartment building complex in Bluebird Circle.
The fire started on the outside of the building, but spread, despite their best effort, to some of the units inside. Seven tenants of the building were displaced because of the fire, and one person was injured as they broke first-floor windows during the incident.
The Maine Department of Public Safety says the State Fire Marshal's Office was called back to the area to investigate Saturday's fire, too, and said that had a little extra caution been taken when someone put out their cigar or cigarette, the fire may have been prevented.
"Investigators from the Maine State Fire Marshal's Office determined the fire was accidental, caused by improper disposal of smoking materials... Cigarettes and other smoking materials should be fully extinguished and discarded in sturdy, noncombustible containers. They should never be discarded in mulch, vegetation, or other combustible materials near buildings."
The same advice should be used for discarding ashes from a fireplace or wood stove, too. Improperly discarded burn materials were the cause of a massive apartment fire in Presque Isle earlier this week.

title: District 2 candidates say they feel confident after months of campaigning
text:
BANGOR, Maine (WABI) - Former Republican Gov. Paul LePage and Democratic state Auditor Matt Dunlap visited polling sites in the 2nd District on Election Day.
One of them will become Maine District 2’s next congressman.
Dunlap, a longtime resident of Old Town, cast his vote at the Elks Lodge on Tuesday morning. LePage was at the Cross Insurance Center in Bangor to greet voters following a stop in Newport.
Both candidates said they feel confident in the race after months of campaigning.
Dunlap on election excitement
Dunlap said he had anticipated higher turnout.
“We had kind of anticipated this to be a higher turnout election just simply because of the energy that’s been demonstrated by people over the last couple of years,” Dunlap said. “All the meetings I’ve gone to for the last year and a half, we’ve had really incredible turnout.”
“When you go to a county committee meeting, typically you’ll see 5 to 10 people there,” Dunlap said. “This year, there usually has not been enough chairs. So I think that has kind of informed what people are thinking about this election cycle and why they’re coming out in such strong numbers to vote.”
LePage on the campaign
“We went around the district from Fort Kent to Fryeburg and we’ve talked to a whole lot of people, taken hundreds and hundreds, if not thousands of pictures and met a lot of people,” LePage said. “And if we win, which I believe we will, we’re going to enjoy it for the next couple days and next Sunday we go to work.”
In a new UNH poll released Sunday, LePage led Dunlap, 52% to 47%. In UNH’s September poll, Dunlap led LePage, 51% to 45%.
Election night plans
LePage will be in Bangor for tonight’s Election Night watch party. Dunlap will be in Old Town. WABI will have live coverage with each candidate.

title: Helicopters collide below Mount Everest base camp, killing 1 person and injuring 2
text:
Helicopters collide below Mount Everest base camp, killing 1 person and injuring 2
Two helicopters collided Tuesday while trying to land just below Mount Everest's base camp, killing at least one person and injuring two others, officials said.
The aircraft were ferrying trekkers who had been hiking up to Everest base camp during Nepal's popular trekking season. Heavy snow had covered the route before the weather improved Sunday and thousands of trekkers were able to move around.
There are no roads on Everest, and helicopters are the only way to bring down trekkers and guides who become sick or exhausted in the cold and high altitude.
The helicopters crashed at Pheriche village, which is at an altitude of 13,780 feet.
A 47-year-old tourist from India was killed in the crash, according to Bhupendra Thapa, a Solukhumbhu district administration officer.
A passenger from New Zealand was injured and was being transported to the capital, Kathmandu, for treatment. A Nepali pilot sustained injuries but was treated locally.
The number of people on the two helicopters wasn't clear.
The Mount Everest base camp trek lasts up to two weeks and goes from the only airstrip in the area at Lukla to base camp located at 17,380 feet.
The trek is popular during the fall season, right after the rainy season and before the harsh winter months.

title: Fort Kent and Wisdom Have Four Chances at Northern Maine Soccer Titles
text:
Four County Teams, Two Schools, One Big Tuesday: Fort Kent and Wisdom Chase Regional Soccer Titles
Four teams. Two schools. One chance to move on to the state championships.
Tuesday could be one of the biggest days of the fall sports season for Fort Kent and Wisdom, with both schools sending their boys and girls soccer teams into Northern Maine regional championship games.
Fort Kent will take over Hampden Academy for the Class C North championships, with both Warrior teams facing Orono.
Meanwhile, Wisdom will head to Brewer High School, where the Pioneers will compete for both Eight-Player North titles against Penobscot Christian and Dexter.
Four championship games, four County teams, and a whole lot on the line.
Here's a look at Tuesday's matchups and how each team got here.
Class C North: Fort Kent Looks for a Championship Sweep
Boys: Fort Kent vs. Orono — 4 p.m.
Location: Hampden Academy
Fort Kent's boys had to survive one of the most dramatic finishes of the semifinal round to earn their place in Tuesday's championship.
The third-seeded Warriors traveled to George Stevens Academy on Saturday and battled the second-seeded Eagles through regulation and overtime.
James Wilson scored Fort Kent's regulation goal, with Dominic Cyr picking up the assist.
With the game tied 1-1 after overtime, the teams headed to penalty kicks.
Fort Kent came through with a 4-2 advantage in the shootout, with Wyatt Daigle delivering the decisive kick to send the Warriors into the regional final.
Now comes another challenge.
Fort Kent enters Tuesday at 9-6-1 and will face an Orono team that has put together an impressive 14-1-1 season.
The Red Riots are the top seed in Class C North, and the Warriors will have to find a way past them to bring home the regional championship.
Fort Kent has already shown it can handle the pressure of a close tournament game.
Tuesday, the stakes get even bigger.
Girls: Fort Kent vs. Orono — 6:30 p.m.
Location: Hampden Academy
A few hours after the boys take the field, Fort Kent's girls will get their opportunity to bring a Class C North championship back to the St. John Valley.
The top-seeded Lady Warriors enter Tuesday at 14-1-2 after a convincing 5-0 semifinal victory over Houlton.
That game was scoreless until the 50th minute, when Reece Doucette converted a penalty kick to put Fort Kent in front.
From there, the Lady Warriors took control.
Doucette finished with two goals, Hayden Plourde added two more, and Avery Werntgen also found the back of the net.
Now Fort Kent will face second-seeded Orono, which enters the championship at 11-4-1.
The Red Riots advanced by surviving a penalty-kick decision against Winslow in the semifinals.
For Fort Kent, it's an opportunity to finish a strong Northern Maine tournament run with a regional championship.
And there's something special about Tuesday's schedule.
Both Fort Kent teams will face the same opponent, on the same field, with Northern Maine titles on the line.
The Warriors could make it a memorable evening for their school and community.
Eight-Player North: Wisdom Has Two Championship Opportunities
Boys: Wisdom vs. Penobscot Christian — 4 p.m.
Location: Brewer High School
Wisdom's boys are coming off a semifinal that won't soon be forgotten.
The third-seeded Pioneers traveled to Calais on Friday and survived a dramatic penalty-kick finish to earn their spot in the Eight-Player North championship.
James Desjardins scored Wisdom's regulation goal before the game eventually went to a shootout.
Preston Lavoie, Sam Paradis, Zeek Cyr and Cayden Hargrove converted penalty kicks for Wisdom.
Then goalkeeper Bentley Nadeau came up with the save that mattered most, stopping Calais' final attempt to secure the victory.
The Pioneers enter Tuesday at 13-3, with a much different kind of challenge waiting.
Penobscot Christian comes in undefeated at 16-0.
PCHS advanced with a 3-0 semifinal victory over Houlton and will be looking to finish its Northern Maine tournament run with another win.
But Wisdom has already shown it can find a way through difficult tournament matchups.
The Pioneers have scoring options, tournament experience and a goalkeeper who just delivered one of the biggest saves of their season.
Now they'll need another complete performance to get past the undefeated Patriots.
Girls: Wisdom vs. Dexter — 6 p.m.
Location: Brewer High School
Wisdom's girls have been one of the most impressive teams in the Eight-Player North tournament.
The second-seeded Lady Pioneers enter Tuesday at 14-2 after handing previously unbeaten Sumner its first loss of the season in Friday's semifinal.
And they didn't just squeak by.
Wisdom rolled to a 5-0 victory, with Ellie Cyr scoring twice and Madi Cyr, Libby Cote and Hannah Martin each adding a goal.
The Lady Pioneers have now scored 11 goals in two tournament games while allowing just one.
That's a pretty good way to enter a regional championship.
Waiting for Wisdom is top-seeded Dexter, which enters at 13-2-1.
The Tigers advanced with a 2-0 semifinal victory over Shead, setting up a meeting between the top two seeds in Eight-Player North.
Wisdom has already knocked off one unbeaten opponent in this tournament.
Now the Lady Pioneers have another opportunity to prove themselves against one of the region's top teams.
And with a state championship berth on the line, there's plenty of motivation for both sides.

title: Midterms may bring in wave of historic firsts for some states and the country
text:
Featuring one of the most diverse slates of both Democratic and Republican candidates in recent years, this midterm election has set up a possible wave of historic leadership firsts across the country.
Voters on Tuesday could propel into office the first Native American female governor and Native women senators, the first Black female governor,the first openly gay U.S. senator and the first Muslim U.S. senator, among other milestones. Most are Democrats, but the GOP could also break ground.
While some of these candidates have avoided focusing on the inherent historic value of their race, gender, religion or sexual orientation, some voters’ rights advocates are celebrating how the electorate has expanded.
“These firsts show how our country is changing,” Alexis Anderson-Reed, president and CEO of State Voices, a network of advocates for civic engagement and equity in democracy, said via e-mail.
“For years, people of color and LGBTQ+ communities have organized, knocked on doors, talked to voters, held conversations, and done the hard work of saving our democracy,” Anderson-Reed said. “These wins are because of them.”
Here are some of the races where history could be made.
First Native American female governor
Democrat Deb Haaland already broke barriers in 2018 as one of the first two Native American women elected to Congress. Then she became the first Native American cabinet secretary, running President Joe Biden’s Department of the Interior. Charles Curtis, from the Kaw Nation, was President Herbert Hoover’s vice president.
Now the Laguna Pueblo citizen is poised to add first Native American woman governor to the list if she beats Republican Gregg Hull, a former mayor, in New Mexico.
Oklahoma is the only state to elect a tribal citizen for governor — Democrat Johnston Murray in the 1950s and current Republican Gov. Kevin Stitt.
Haaland shrugged off a question about her various political identities in a recent interview with The Associated Press.
“I mean, somebody has to be the first,” she said. “I just don’t want to be the last, right?”
But she says she’s proud to see how Indigenous people care about representation as other Native women run. “It truly does matter,” Haaland said. “It’s not just a slogan.”
First Native woman senators
Mary Peltola, who is Yup’ik and a Democrat, was considered a trailblazer in 2022 when she became the first Alaska Native elected to the U.S. House of Representatives. Now the former congresswoman is trying to do the same in the Senate by unseating Republican incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan.
The honor could also go to Minnesota Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan, a progressive Democrat and a citizen of the White Earth Band of Ojibwe who faces Republican Michele Tafoya, a former NFL sideline reporter.
And if Tafoya wins, she too would make history — as the first Republican of Latina heritage to sit in the U.S. Senate.
First Black female governor
Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms and Republican Lisa Demuth could end a 250-year streak without a Black woman serving as a state’s governor.
Bottoms, the former Atlanta mayor, is running against Republican Rick Jackson, a billionaire businessman, to be governor of Georgia. If she wins, Bottoms would also be Georgia’s first governor of color. All 83 of Georgia’s previous governors have been white men.
Demuth, the former Minnesota House speaker, is going up against longtime Minnesota U.S. Sen. Amy Klobuchar. Whatever the outcome, Minnesota will get its first female governor.
Stacey Abrams is the only Black woman to come close to winning a governor’s race when she got the Georgia Democratic Party’s nomination in 2018 and 2022.
First Muslim U.S. senator
Abdul El-Sayed could be the first Muslim American to serve in the U.S. Senate.
The progressive Michigan Democrat needs to defeat Republican Mike Rogers in what has been a very tight and contentious race.
El-Sayed has had to contend with Republicans all the way up to Trump implying or overtly stating that the Michigan-born epidemiologist is not American and supports terrorism. Trump has called him “dangerously radical,” “too extreme” and referred to him as “Mohammed.” El-Sayed and his supporters have denounced the attacks as Islamophobic or racist affronts to religious freedom.
First openly gay U.S. senator
Democratic Rep. Chris Pappas could be the country’s first openly gay senator if he’s elected in New Hampshire. He is running against former Republican U.S. Sen. John E. Sununu.
Pappas already became the first openly gay member of Congress when he was elected in 2018.
This potential new benchmark is not something Pappas has dwelled on while campaigning, saying “I’m not running to make history.” But he also applauded the fact that his sexual orientation was not a huge source of discussion among potential voters.
First Black governors
The U.S. could go from having only three elected Black governors in its 250-year history to gaining seven more overnight.
Maryland Gov. Wes Moore, the third one in the U.S. and the only current Black governor, is projected to win re-election. Besides Georgia and Minnesota, he could also have new peers in Florida, Wisconsin, Nevada, South Carolina and Michigan.
Moore, chair of the National Governors Association, has called the presence of so many Black gubernatorial contenders “a unique moment.” It’s not “an applause line” but a challenge to make diverse gubernatorial nominees more common, he said.
Record year of women running for governor and Congress
This midterm has been a record-breaker for women vying for state and federal offices. Democrats increased their 2022 number of women candidates to 19 running for governor, according to the Center for American Women and Politics at Rutgers University. The Republican Party has seven women setting their sights on governor.
Like Minnesota, Tennessee will elect its first female governor. The main candidates are Republican U.S. Sen. Marsha Blackburn and Democrat Jerri Green, a Memphis city councilwoman.
The election of the first Democratic Asian American woman as governor could happen in Vermont with Amanda Janoo, who is half Malaysian, or Oklahoma with Cyndi Munson, a former state lawmaker of Korean descent. Former Republican Gov. Nikki Haley of South Carolina, who is of Indian heritage, was the first Asian American female governor.
Nearly 300 women, including incumbents, are running for the U.S. Senate and House, as documented by Rutgers’ Center for American Women and Politics.
Among them is Democrat Juliana Stratton in Illinois. If Stratton, who is Black, wins her Senate race, then she and fellow Democrat Sen. Tammy Duckworth, who is of Thai heritage, will make Illinois the first state to be represented by two female senators of color.
____
Associated Press writers Becky Bohrer in Juneau, Alaska, and Savannah Peters in Albuquerque, New Mexico, contributed to this report.
